text:
jess: @sam heads-up: AcmeInc complaining about p95/p99 jumps since ~09:35 UTC, p99s ~8-12s, some 503s. sample req ids: req=acm-9f3, req=acm-9f7. Customer says it started right after their traffic spike.

sam: looking now — can you paste a minimal repro and the request-id?

jess: paste from customer: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" -H \"X-Request-ID: acm-9f3\" -d \"{\\\"prompt\\\":\\\"hello\\\"}\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` . They said timeouts on retries.

customer-bot: Customer AcmeInc flagged priority: high, org: acme-inc, contact: ops@acme.com

sam: seeing deploy-bot event around 09:30 — `deploy-bot: rollout inference-runtime v2.4.1 -> prod (canary 15%) at 09:30 UTC` — not sure if related.

maya: infra metrics: ingress queue length spiked at 09:35 -> 09:42. max_queue=430, avg_inflight_per_shard=12 -> then some shards dropped to 0 because admission controller started shedding. p95 correlates with queue depth. snippet:```metric: ingress.queue_length 09:32=12 09:35=430 09:38=312 09:42=40```

oncall: @maya any signs of hot restart or OOMs?

maya: no OOMs. scheduler logs show `admission: reject tenant acme-inc reason=concurrency_cap` repeatedly. The tenant's concurrency cap is 50. Their burst sent ~200 concurrent requests from one region -> queues filled and admission started fast-failing.

sam: got it. So this is tenant-level fairness + admission threshold. Are we auto-failing over to smaller model or a fallback route?

li: product note — AcmeInc uses model `redwood-large` for majority of traffic and has aggressive client-side retries. No fallback enabled in their route.

jess: customer ops says they retried aggressively which made pileup worse (retry storm).

sam: mitigation options: 1) temp increase per-tenant concurrency cap for acme-inc to 200, 2) enable fast-fail for retries (quota throttle), 3) route their requests to a lower-cost instance group or smaller model `redwood-medium` as fallback.

oncall: preference is quick config change first. @maya can you bump acme-inc cap and monitor?

maya: applying change now: `curl -X POST https://internal-admin.redwood/v1/tenants/acme-inc/settings -d '{"concurrency_cap":200}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer admin-token'` -> applied at 09:52 UTC.

sam: noticed queue length dropped after ~60s. p99 falling back. telemetry: p99 10s -> 1.2s in 2 mins.

jess: customer ops updated: they see normal latency now.

maya: follow-ups: we should add automatic per-tenant temporary-burst allowance to avoid abrupt shedding, and add a circuit-breaker on retries to cap retry attempts per request-id. Also instrument per-tenant inflight histogram.

li: agree — product will track change. We'll add a prompt to onboarding docs about enabling fallback models and soft quota limits.

sam: root cause summary: sudden client-side burst + aggressive retries hit tenant concurrency cap -> admission controller shed traffic -> queue pileup + higher p95/p99 and some 503s. Not a runtime bug; behavior is by-design fairness.

jess: action items: (1) maya to add per-tenant burst window proposal PR (#3812), (2) sam to add a short-term metric alert for ingress.queue_length per-tenant, (3) li to propose onboarding doc update.

maya: created PR draft at https://git.redwood/internal/pr/3812, added notes.

oncall: closing for now — reached out to AcmeInc ops to confirm. If they see recurrence reopen. :thumbsup:

jess: thanks everyone, marking as resolved with follow-up task in Jira.

customer-bot: AcmeInc: thanks for the quick response, latency back to normal on our side.

sam: post-mortem scheduled tomorrow 10:00 UTC to decide permanent mitigations.```
